II21A-01.note: A restates the near/far pattern the passage says both accounts fit, and D contradicts it, so both fall without reasoning; B/C is a reversed pair decided by the final sentence (upslope warmer and drier). B is the tempting slip for a reader who maps 'spring' to 'warm'.

II21A-02.note: Three habitats must be combined: pools vs riffles holds crayfish constant and varies oxygen, so a difference weakens the crayfish account. D (pools vs backwaters) is the most tempting because it shares the 'pools' anchor but actually supports Dufresne; C weakens Barreto, not Dufresne; B fits both.

II21A-03.note: A restates the north/south difference both accounts fit and C contradicts it, so the item reduces to the B/D reversed pair decided by one sentence (channel has pike, bays have weeds). B is tempting for a reader who links weeds to depth generally.

II21A-04.note: Drops: Corlan 6, Bexa 9, Dalmi 8, Elsin 13; 'every greenhouse variety' needs the strongest greenhouse competitor, Dalmi. D (Farrel) is a field variety and falls on sight; A (Bexa) is the tempting near-miss. Test-wise 'pick the closest competitor' rule applies, but the drop must still be computed.

II21A-05.note: Only C compares a pond with backswimmers to one without; A, B and D are same-group comparisons that die on one glance at the first column. The temperature control (Cobb warmer yet fewer larvae) is a nice touch but not needed to pick C.

II21A-06.note: Fractions retained: Corvane 0.80, Abrisk 0.75, Eskelin 0.65, Belloway 0.60, Dunmarra 0.50; Abrisk is the closest competitor. A student comparing absolute salt-water mass rejects A (45 > 40), which is a good discriminating trap; B and D also tempt on absolute values.

II21B-01.note: D restates the age/cracking link both fit and B contradicts it; A/C reversed pair decided by the last sentence (valley: more freezing, less traffic). Same two-confound template as A-01 and A-03.

II21B-02.note: D restates the late-summer peak both fit and B contradicts it; A/C reversed pair decided by the northern-bays sentence. C is tempting for a reader who reaches for warm water = more algae.

II21B-03.note: Hollows collect CO2 but are moister, so ridges dying more points to drought. A supports Haskins (the tempting reversal in direction), B fits both, C (tree age) is beside the point.

II21B-04.note: Specific energy: prototype 150, H 120, J 140, K 230, L 160 Wh/kg. A compares to a sodium-ion cell (beside the claim) and C is visibly larger on sight (more energy, less mass); D requires dividing 360/2.25 and is the real trap.

II21B-05.note: Only Hallam Depot is a white membrane roof among the options; A, B, D are other surfaces and die on the label column. B (Kiln Lab, closest value 69) is the most tempting. C shows only the stronger of the two membrane roofs, which suffices but does not literally show 'either'.

II21B-06.note: Requires classifying stations against the 1,400 m pool top: D pairs an above-pool station with a lower within-pool station and the higher is milder. C is the reversed cross-boundary pair (within-pool milder) and is the strongest trap; B is within-pool only; A is above-pool only and falls fairly quickly.

II21C-01.note: D restates the old/new pattern both fit and B contradicts it; A/C reversed pair decided by the Marwick/Ronsdale sentence. Same confound-splitting template again; A tempts a reader who mixes up which district rents.

II21C-02.note: Renfield isolates confusion (moved, same distance), so Mosby > Renfield shows distance adds decline beyond confusion. D (Mosby vs Ordway) is the most tempting because it shows a distance-linked decline but confounds distance with change; B supports Ortega; C weakens Moraes. Breaks the reversed-pair template, which is good.

II21C-03.note: C restates the casual/formal pattern both fit and D contradicts it; A/B reversed pair decided by the council/market sentence. A tempts a reader anchored on 'casual = more dropping'.

II21C-04.note: Under-100 cooperatives: Neddick 0.55, Pruett 0.45, Quarles 0.70; the closest competitor is Pruett. A (Marlow, 310 members) is outside the comparison set and C is the extreme value; B is the tempting under-100 near-miss.

II21C-05.note: The highest standard classroom is Redvale (76). C (Mercer) is a visual-models classroom outside the comparison set and A is the extreme low value; D (Norcott, 74) is the tempting near-miss. Same 'closest competitor in the named group' template as A-04, A-06, C-04.

II21C-06.note: Only Ostler (17 < 19) fell below half among program neighborhoods. B (Northby, 40 to 16) is the most tempting because it does fall below half, but it is not in the program; A and D need a quick half-check.

II21D-01.note: D restates the over-time rise both fit and B contradicts it; A/C reversed pair decided by the upland/lowland sentence. The reversed-pair-plus-time-pair template recurs in A-01, A-03, B-01, B-02, C-01, C-03, D-01.

II21D-02.note: Sorle lower (mild floods, salt) vs Tyrne upper (violent floods, no salt) is the only pair that sets the two factors against each other. B and C are within-river lower>upper comparisons that fit both since floods also grow downstream; D fits both. Strong item.

II21D-03.note: D holds storage constant (both dry) and varies the iron mill. B is the tempting trap: Wyrlow vs Tamsby but confounded by damp vs dry. A supports Yarrow; C compares two wooden-beater mills and falls on sight.

II21D-04.note: B compares south vs north within one decade, controlling for age. A is the tempting trap (south vs north but different decades); C and D vary age within one orientation. Sannick vs Torbel would also work but is not offered.

II21D-05.note: Highest installment novel is Tidewater (7,800). A (Vesper Lane) is a complete volume, outside the comparison set and the closest value; D is the extreme low. C (Yewfield Hall) is the near-miss.

II21D-06.note: Gains among never-Sunday libraries: Tolvane +60, Wexmoor +120, Zaltby -40; Wexmoor is the strongest competitor. A and B are Sunday-opening libraries and fall on the first column; D (Tolvane, larger starting count) tempts a reader comparing end totals.
